chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought shares of the butchers before the share was drawn, so he said: 'He should not buy anything until he knows where the share will fall. If he bought something, then he has the option (to keep or return it) when it falls.'

key_terms.الْخِيَارِ: The option/right to choose (to keep or return)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying lottery shares before the draw is complete?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of *al-qirash* (lottery-style sales) in meat distribution, emphasizing that uncertainty (*gharar*) is mitigated by either knowing the outcome beforehand or retaining the right of option (*khiyar al-shart*) upon its revelation. It highlights the Shia juristic focus on fairness in communal resource allocation, ensuring buyers are not bound by chance until the specific asset is identified. This principle underscores the broader Islamic legal objective of preventing exploitation in speculative transactions.
